clue.text: Order requiring no attention

parts.note: a parade-ground command that releases soldiers from standing stiffly to attention

explanation.surface: An instruction that nobody needs to heed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention' reads as general heed, but it is the drill position this command relaxes.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a military command telling troops to relax from the rigid drill posture.

clue.text: Moment in time to take a staple food

parts.note: rice is a staple food for much of the world

explanation.surface: A moment taken in time to eat a basic dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant, a very short moment, as in 'in a ___'.

clue.text: Wrote some music, no little thanks to Mr. Heath

parts.note: taken as written
ta is a short informal British thank-you
Ted Heath was the British prime minister of the early 1970s

explanation.surface: A composer thanks the prime minister, not much.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath, Conservative prime minister 1970-74, was also a keen musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down music in written form is to write it.

clue.text: Means a go-between

definitions.meaning: the method or instrumentality by which something happens
a business acting on behalf of others, an intermediary

explanation.surface: It denotes an intermediary.
explanation.definitionFit: Instrumentality is a means; an intermediary firm or bureau acts between parties.

clue.text: Expand a tricky case long delayed

indicators.note: a tricky arrangement is a twisted one, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: late means long delayed

explanation.surface: A complicated legal case dragged on and grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges CASE into ESCA, then LATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase or intensify is to expand.

clue.text: Separate a number-and then some

definitions.meaning: distinct or individual, as in 'went their ___ ways'
more than two but not many, a number and more

explanation.surface: Dividing out a quantity and a bit more.
explanation.definitionFit: Respective or distinct is separate; more than a couple is a handful.

clue.text: Born with a silver spoon in the mouth, for example

definitions.text: Born with a silver spoon in the mouth, for example

parts.words: Born with a silver spoon in the mouth, for example
parts.note: read as a novice's good fortune at the very start of life

explanation.surface: Someone born into a rich family.
explanation.walkthrough: A silver spoon means inherited wealth; a baby is a beginner, so this is fortune that comes at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearned success at the outset is the fortune of novices.

clue.text: Insect only efts can consume

indicators.note: the letters are digested and churned up, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A creature that only newts are able to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This winged insect lives near streams and is used as fishing bait.

clue.text: One who goes to work in style

definitions.text: One who goes to work in style

parts.words: One who goes to work in style
parts.note: a person whose job is creating fashionable clothes, working in the field of style

explanation.surface: Someone who commutes elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to work in style' seems to describe a smart commuter; it means a person whose work is style.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion creator works in clothing styles.

clue.text: A bull extraordinarily cited

indicators.note: doing something extraordinarily means doing it out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quoted a bull in some unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull here is a papal bull, a formal decree from the Pope, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal bull is an official decree issued by the Pope.

clue.text: It's down-to earth and may provide a tax cover

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder may be rearranged to provide the answer, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Something practical that might shelter you from tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-to earth' looks like 'practical', but it means a machine that goes down into the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A digging machine sends its bucket down into the ground.

clue.text: Nice lad it may turn out, all the same

indicators.note: how the letters may turn out when rearranged signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A pleasant boy might prove himself regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the same' reads as 'nevertheless', but it means exactly alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are exactly alike are all the same.

clue.text: Encompassing cartels

parts.note: price-fixing groups of traders, pictured as circles that surround

explanation.surface: Business groups that take in everything around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartels of dealers are called rings, and a ring is a shape that encircles.

clue.text: One lacking substance such as Mr. Pooter

definitions.meaning: an insignificant person of no importance
Charles Pooter is the hero of the comic novel The Diary of a ___ by the Grossmith brothers

explanation.surface: A lightweight person like the suburban clerk of the comic diary.
explanation.definitionFit: An unimportant person is a cipher; Pooter is the title character of Grossmith's Victorian diary novel.

clue.text: It shouldn't be a spineless response

definitions.text: It shouldn't be a spineless response

parts.words: It shouldn't be a spineless response
parts.note: an impudent reply needs a back, so it cannot come from a spineless person

explanation.surface: A reply ought to show some courage.
explanation.walkthrough: A spine is the back, so a cheeky retort is talk with some back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent retorts answering back are insolence from someone with backbone.

clue.text: Ate like a horse in a stable

definitions.text: Ate like a horse in a stable

parts.words: Ate like a horse in a stable
parts.note: describes livestock fattened indoors in a stall rather than at pasture

explanation.surface: Someone ate greedily, like a horse in its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ate like a horse' suggests greed, but it is literal: fed in a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals fattened on fodder in a stall, not at grass, are so described.

clue.text: Western Hemisphere discovery

parts.note: the Americas, found by Europeans in Columbus's time

explanation.surface: Something found on the western side of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas were called this by Europeans after Columbus reached them.

clue.text: Transport in colour adapted for further use

indicators.note: the transport word sits inside the colour word

parts.note: red is a colour
a cycle (bicycle) is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle painted a colour was converted for more use.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste material reprocessed is used again.

clue.text: The character of a bore

definitions.meaning: quality or standard of a person
the internal diameter of a gun barrel

explanation.surface: What a tedious person is like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person, but it is a gun's barrel width.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth or quality of mind, and also the inner diameter of a gun barrel.

clue.text: Dolly's place in the City

indicators.note: to place the letters afresh is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Where Dolly lives in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, home of the famous insurance market.
explanation.definitionFit: The insurance market is based in the Square Mile, London's financial district.

clue.text: Free translation of braille

indicators.note: translating the word converts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A loose rendering of the raised-dot script for the blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous or unrestricted, as in a loose version not bound by the original.

clue.text: Get out and continue to bat

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batsman who deflects the ball onto his own stumps is out this way

explanation.surface: A cricketer is dismissed yet keeps batting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the phrase also means edging the ball onto one's own wicket and being bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it means dismissing oneself by deflecting onto the wicket; generally it means carry on.

clue.text: In the vicinity of San Pablo, California

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Near a town in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearby is in the neighbourhood.

clue.text: The benefit of one enjoying good health

parts.note: someone well is in good health
a being is a living creature, one individual

explanation.surface: A healthy person's advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare or benefit is a person's good state.

clue.text: A youngster introduce to an epic

parts.note: A, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: one piece is introduced into the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
an, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Bringing a child into contact with a long heroic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is a classic heroic epic.

clue.text: Saucy little fruit

parts.note: a small red berry best known as a sauce served with turkey

explanation.surface: A cheeky small piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' seems to mean cheeky, but it means made into a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: This tart red berry is famously made into sauce for roast turkey.

clue.text: Put up for a rise in America

definitions.meaning: Americans call a pay increase by this name where Britons say a rise

explanation.surface: Offered in return for a pay increase in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift is to put up; US English names a salary increase this way.

clue.text: Brownie Guider's star role

parts.note: a woman guiding young Brownies is literally one at the front; also the main female part in a play

explanation.surface: The chief part played by the adult running a Brownie pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior Girl Guides; their adult leader is a woman who leads.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal actress in a show takes the top female part.
